title: Step Therapy Clinical Policy — Utilization Management Program
content:
## Policy

A step therapy target under the Utilization Management Program is covered once the member has tried the protocol's prerequisites: at least the protocol's required number of different prerequisite drugs, each with at least the package's minimum trial days supply in Northbridge Rx claims history within the package's step look-back days before the date the step is evaluated. The required number is the protocol entry's own count.

A member with a paid claim for the target drug itself within the package's grandfathering days before the claim date is exempt from the step.

When the package checks the step automatically and the history satisfies the step (or the member is grandfathered), the approval is recorded automatically when the drug is billed, as an auto-approved case event when the package records automated approvals that way; otherwise a step therapy exception case is needed.

A step therapy exception case is approved with *criteria met* when the trials are found in claims history, when the prescriber documents trials outside Northbridge Rx history (another carrier's claims or samples) with dates and days supply, or when every prerequisite is contraindicated; otherwise it is denied with *step not satisfied*.

An automated step approval may be recorded only when the claims history satisfies the step or the member is grandfathered. The authority for that is the system's claims records for the member and the target drug, not the member's account of past use.

## How the history is measured

- **Trials.** Over the look-back window — the package's step look-back days ending on the date the step is evaluated, that date counted as day zero — the trials are the number of distinct prerequisite drugs of the target's protocol for which the member's paid, unreversed retail claims, shipped home delivery orders and shipped specialty fills add up to at least the minimum trial days supply. The step is satisfied when that number is at least the protocol's required number of different prerequisites.
- **Grandfathering.** Over the package's grandfathering days ending on the claim date (claim date as day zero), the member is grandfathered when at least one paid, unreversed claim for the target drug itself exists — retail, home delivery or specialty.

## Hypothetical illustrations

| Situation (hypothetical; 180-day look-back, 30-day minimum, 1 prerequisite required) | Trials counted | Step satisfied |
|---|---|---|
| metformin: two paid retail claims of 15 days supply each inside the window | 1 | Yes |
| metformin: one paid claim of 30 days supply, later reversed | 0 | No |
| metformin: shipped home delivery order of 90 days supply 200 days before the evaluation date | 0 | No |

For a protocol requiring 2 different prerequisites, a history showing a full trial of only one of them gives 1 trial and does not satisfy the step.
